paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to take from this one. Bartimaeus had no way to see Jesus, but he could hear that Jesus was close, and he did something about it. He cried out, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!" (Mark 10:47). That's the whole prayer, and it's a good one: say who He is, ask for mercy, and don't wait until you've got your words polished.

Now watch what happens when the crowd pushes back. "Many people admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder" (Mark 10:48). Friend, there will be voices telling you to keep it down, and some of them will be your own. Bartimaeus shows us that the answer is to keep calling out to Jesus. And Jesus stopped for that voice and said, "Call him" (Mark 10:49). He wasn't too busy, and the crowd wasn't too big.

Then Jesus asks him, "What do you want Me to do for you?" (Mark 10:51). He asks, even though it's plain to see what Bartimaeus needs. So you can bring Jesus the real request, out loud, like Bartimaeus did. And look at the end: he "received his sight and followed Jesus along the road" (Mark 10:52). When Jesus gives mercy, a baker's best answer is to follow Him, and I can tell you from my own kitchen that this is the best road to be on.
